name: discovery
title: Discovery
description: What there is to play, and the way into it. One tile per game, each carrying `data-gs-availability` for which of three things is true of it: live, upcoming, or ended. That is host-declared, because the library holds no clock, so an upcoming game whose countdown reaches zero stays upcoming until the host says otherwise. A tile is not a choice: picking one is not answering a question, so it carries `data-gs-item` and never `data-gs-choice`, `data-gs-selected` or `data-gs-committed`. Each tile has one control whose label is the verb of its outcome, and every control's accessible name carries the game's name, because four tiles offering "Join" are four identical controls to anyone reading them out. The art is a node the host supplies; a tile without it keeps a filled media area rather than showing a blank rectangle. It performs nothing: it fetches no list, opens nothing, and remembers no reminder.
docs: Pass `games` in the order you want them shown and `label` as the list's accessible name. Set each game's `availability` yourself and update it when your own clock says so; the component never changes it. Pass `art` as a node, an `img` or a poster of your own, and leave it out when you have none. Pass `featured` to render the first game as a full-width hero tile. Pass `availabilityWords` to translate live, starts soon and ended. Render an `empty-state` in place of this component when there is nothing to list, and an `error-state` when the list failed to load: discovery shows games and says nothing about why there are none.
